sections.h2: Which Darke County offices handle your property tax?
sections.html:
Two courthouse offices split the work: the county auditor sets values and hears the paperwork on exemptions, and the county treasurer sends the bills and takes the payments. Both sit on the first floor of the Darke County Courthouse at 504 S. Broadway in Greenville, and both keep weekday hours of 8:00 am to 4:00 pm.

The auditor also runs the county's real estate website, where you can search a parcel, view the map, pull a sales report, run a delinquency report and use a tax estimator and a conveyance fee calculator. The same site holds the downloadable forms discussed below.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Darke County for a house sale?
sections.html:
Darke County is a rural county in western Ohio along the Indiana line, with Greenville as the county seat and only city. The county covers about 600 square miles, and the 2020 census counted 51,881 residents, with 71.7 percent of them living in rural areas.

The same census count lists 22,599 housing units, of which 7.4 percent were vacant, and 73.4 percent of occupied homes were owner-occupied. A high owner share and a large amount of farmland shape the tax questions here: many sellers hold acreage, outbuildings or a house on a split-off lot, and each of those touches a different tax rule.

  • Houses inside the villages and the city of Greenville sit in school districts such as Greenville City, Versailles Exempted Village, Ansonia Local and Arcanum-Butler Local.
  • The county sits next to Montgomery County on its southeast side, so some owners commute toward Dayton.
  • Manufacturing is the largest employment sector, at 26.6 percent of annual employment in a state profile cited on the county's Wikipedia page.

sections.h2: How often does Darke County reappraise property?
sections.html:
The county page for the auditor says the auditor directs a general reappraisal of real property every six years, with an update in the third year after each reappraisal. Between those cycles your value changes only for new construction, demolition, splits or a Board of Revision order.

The auditor's website posts a duplicate of valuations for each tax year, including the one billed in 2027, plus a page of tax rates by year. Those rates differ by taxing district, so the same house value gives a different bill in Greenville than in a village school district. Use the tax estimator on the auditor's site, then ask the auditor's real estate division which district a parcel sits in.

sections.h2: When are Darke County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Ohio law lets a taxpayer pay the full year by December 31 or pay half by that date and the rest by June 20 (ORC 323.12), and a payment counts if the treasurer receives it or if the envelope carries a United States Postal Service postmark by the last day. A private meter mark does not count.

Ask the Darke County treasurer for the dates printed on the current bill, since the treasurer may hold the books open a little longer for a collection period. The treasurer's office takes online payments through the tax payment cart on the real estate site.

  • If a lender escrows your taxes, tell the lender you received a copy of the bill.
  • If you are behind, run the delinquency report on the auditor's site and call the treasurer for a payoff figure before you list the house.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Darke County valuation?
sections.html:
File a complaint on the state form DTE 1 with the county auditor, who passes it to the Board of Revision. The deadline under ORC 5715.19 is March 31 of the following tax year, or the close of first-half collection if that is later.

The form is on the Darke auditor's forms page, along with the Board of Revision rules of practice and a separate form (DTE 2) for complaints about something other than market value. A few points from the statute matter for sellers.

  • Say what value you claim. The complaint must state the amount of the alleged overvaluation.
  • You may pay tax on your claimed value while the case is pending, and the treasurer must accept that tender. If the final value is higher, interest accrues on the difference.
  • After an earlier complaint, a repeat filing in the same reappraisal period is allowed only for changes such as an arm's-length sale, casualty loss or a major improvement.
  • The board must hear an original complaint within 180 days after the filing deadline and give at least ten days' notice of the hearing.
  • Bring every piece of evidence you hold. Evidence withheld at the board can be barred on appeal.

sections.h2: Which tax breaks can Darke County owners use?
sections.html:
Three programs come up most: the homestead reduction, the owner-occupied residence reduction, and the farmland valuation. Each has its own application form on the auditor's website.

For homestead, the auditor's question page says you must be 65 by December 31 of the application year, permanently and totally disabled on January 1, or a qualifying surviving spouse who was at least 59 when the spouse died. You must own the home and live in it as your main residence on January 1. The page lists an income cap of $40,000 for 2024 applicants, indexed upward each year, and it says the credit equals the tax on $28,000 of true value. Ask the auditor for the current year's limit. Apply on form DTE 105A, and file the disability certificate DTE 105E if that applies. A late application for the prior year is accepted until December 31.

Farmland can be valued at its current agricultural use through application DTE 109. Under ORC 5713.30 the land must be at least ten acres in commercial agricultural use for the three years before filing, or under ten acres with average yearly gross income of at least $2,500. If a sale ends that status, a recoupment charge for the tax savings can follow.

sections.h2: What happens with the tax when a Darke County house sells?
sections.html:
Before the deed goes to the recorder, the buyer files a conveyance fee statement with the auditor (form DTE 100, or DTE 100EX when an exemption applies). The seller pays the conveyance fee and any county transfer tax at that stage, and the auditor stamps the deed.

The statement also asks about homestead and farmland. If the buyer's side of the form shows that the property carried a homestead or owner-occupancy reduction, the parties must account for how that reduction ends, and a farm sale needs the matching statement on form DTE 102 when the land was under agricultural valuation. The auditor's site has a conveyance fee calculator that adds the parcel transfer fee.

If any tax is delinquent, ask the treasurer for a payoff figure so the title company can include it in the closing numbers.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Darke County?
faqs.a: The Darke County Treasurer bills and collects the tax. The auditor sets the value on which the bill is based. Call the treasurer at 937-547-7365 about a bill, and the auditor's real estate division at 937-547-7308 about a value.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to dispute my Darke County value?
faqs.a: The deadline is March 31 of the following tax year, or the close of first-half collection if that date is later. File form DTE 1 with the county auditor, who forwards it to the Board of Revision.

faqs.q: Does Darke County offer a senior tax reduction?
faqs.a: Yes, through the Ohio homestead program for owners who are 65 or older, permanently disabled, or qualifying surviving spouses. File DTE 105A with the auditor and ask what income limit applies to the current year.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Darke County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Ask the treasurer for a payoff figure and use the delinquency report on the auditor's website to see what is listed.

faqs.q: Where do I find the Darke County tax rate for my parcel?
faqs.a: Look at the tax rates page on the auditor's forms list or run the tax estimator on the real estate website. Rates vary by taxing district, so confirm your district with the auditor's real estate division.
